text:
Kai: Heads up — around 05:12 UTC we saw a huge burst of GPU job submissions to the spot pool in us-west1. Cluster-autoscaler spawned ~8 small GPU nodes in parallel, then ~15 mins later they were all drained and scaled down. Some jobs ended up Pending for >10m due to packing fragmentation.
Marin: saw the same. pods had strict nodeAffinity + gpu resource requests, and we ended up with 2 nodes with 1 GPU each and several pods waiting even though aggregate capacity existed.
Sam: this smells like binpacking + CA scale-up granularity. Did we get any preemption events during that window?
ops-bot: incident detected: Spot pool "gpu-spot-usw1" scale activity spike 05:10–05:30 UTC, scaleUpCount=8, scaleDownCount=7, preemptions=3.
Anya: preemptions were low, most pods stayed, but scheduler couldn't place them because pods request fractional CPU + full GPU which leaves CPU holes. The autoscaler created nodes that matched GPU count but not sufficient CPU/memory balance.
Kai: cost note — because of the rapid add/remove we also spilled into the on-demand fallback pool for ~6 minutes which increased hour usage by ~0.05 GPU-hours. Not huge but visible in billing dashboards.
Marin: current autoscaler flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=5m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m, expander=least-waste. Maybe least-waste encourages creating many small nodes that fit the immediate request.
Sam: curious — if we switch expander to "random" or use binpacking with balanced instance types could reduce fragmentation. Also thought: increase --max-empty-bulk-delete to avoid immediate churn?
Anya: we should also tune nodepool instance types. Right now gpu-spot-usw1 mixes A100-40GB and A100-80GB; scheduler prefers smaller nodes first, but our pod resource shapes vary. Proposal: split into two pools by instance size and use nodeAffinity for big-batch jobs.
Kai: operational mitigation suggestion: add a short cooldown window to let CA settle before falling back to on-demand. Example: guard fallback route with a 3m window and require >2 consecutive scaleDown events before hitting fallback.
Marin: also saw kube-proxy logs show connection churn during scale events in that AZ — possibly due to rapid IP allocation and SNAT table churn. Might be contributing to some job restarts.
Sam: technical action items I can do now: 1) change expander to "binpacking" on a canary cluster, 2) add --scale-down-unneeded-time=8m, 3) increase scaleDownDelayAfterAdd to 15m. Any objections?
Anya: +1 for canary. Also add a deterministic placement label: job-type=batch-large -> prefer nodepool=a100-80. We'll add toleration/affinity in job templates.
Kai: can we add a graceful termination hook to the worker pods so they checkpoint earlier? Some pods were getting SIGTERM and timing out. Set terminationGracePeriodSeconds=120 and trap SIGTERM in the entrypoint.
Sam: will push kube manifest change for grace period and update our image to handle SIGTERM (flush partial checkpoint).
ops-bot: runbook note created: "spot-burst-handling" with steps to flip autoscaler expander on canary and rollback criteria. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-burst-handling
Anya: longer-term: consider a small warm pool of 1-2 reserved GPUs in each region (on-demand) that CA can use as immediate capacity to avoid hitting fallback routes during spikes. Cost tradeoff vs reduced job latency.
Kai: agree. Let's prototype warm-pool in us-west1 with a monthly cap and evaluate 2 weeks. If bump in cost < 2% but tail latency improves it's worth it.
Sam: I'll create a PR with the autoscaler flag changes and a separate PR for nodepool split (a100-small / a100-large). Will also add a canary label so we can flip it for 10% of traffic.
Marin: for observability: add a per-pod label for "requested-gpu-cpu-shape" so we can plot placement failures by resource shape. That will help tune instance mixes.
eng-infra-oncall: I'll take the oncall followup — monitor spot-eviction-rate and fallback pool ingress for the next 48h. If fallback >3x baseline or pending>5m spikes recur, roll back changes.
Kai: TL;DR action list: Sam -> autoscaler canary PR + SIGTERM handling. Anya -> warm-pool cost proposal and nodeAffinity changes. Marin -> placement labels and scheduler debug. Oncall -> 48h monitoring. ops-bot -> attach runbook to thread.
Sam: PR draft opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k8s-configs/pull/742 (autoscaler expander canary + flags).
Anya: creating warm-pool draft doc and rough cost calc, will link when ready.
Kai: thanks team. We'll reconvene after 48h metrics. :thumbsup:
